identity.title: Mutational binding assessment for TCR engineering on experimental and AlphaFold 3 scaffolds.

content.abstract: Machine learning-based binding affinity prediction can support T-cell receptor (TCR) engineering, but its reliability remains uncertain when experimental structures of TCRs bound to peptide-major histocompatibility complexes (pMHCs) are unavailable and predicted structures must be used instead. Here, we examined how AlphaFold 3 (AF3) scaffold choice and conformational sampling affect DeltaDeltaG -based prioritization of TCR-pMHC complementarity-determining region (CDR) mutations. Bound-unbound structural comparisons showed that pMHC binding is associated mainly with local CDR remodeling, especially in CDR3 loops, whereas TCR framework regions remain comparatively stable. AF3 generally recovered bound-like TCR conformations, but downstream DeltaDeltaG prediction performance depended strongly on both scaffold source and model architecture. These scaffold-dependent differences indicate that experimental structures remain the most reliable input when available, although such structures are rarely accessible in prospective TCR design settings. Among AF3-based inputs, Prompt-DDG and RDE-PPI were relatively robust to wild-type predicted scaffolds, whereas BA-DDG and H3-DDG benefited more from mutant-specific AF3 scaffolds evaluated by reverse-mutation scoring. Across four templates, AF3-mutant scaffolds gave the highest mean top-10 recovery among the AF3-based inputs for all four predictors. These results support using experimental structures when available and suggest using AF3-mutant scaffolds for recovering top-ranked CDR candidates when only predicted structures are available.
